A content delivery network, or CDN, is a system of computers spread across many cities and countries that work together to deliver websites and videos faster. Without one, every request for a photo, video, or webpage would travel all the way back to a single origin server — the original computer where that content is permanently stored. If many people around the world are requesting content at once, that single server gets overloaded, and people far away experience slow loading because data must travel a long physical distance.

A CDN solves this by placing copies of popular content on many smaller computers positioned closer to where people actually are. Each of these nearby computers is called an edge location, since it sits at the edge of the network, near the audience rather than near the original server. When someone requests a file and it is already stored on a nearby edge location, that is called a cache hit — the request is answered instantly from a nearby copy instead of traveling far away. Think of it like a chain of neighborhood libraries that each keep copies of the most popular books, so most readers never need to travel downtown to the central archive. Only when a requested file is not yet stored nearby does the edge location fetch it from the origin server, then keep a copy for next time. This arrangement makes streaming, browsing, and downloading feel fast and reliable for millions of people simultaneously, no matter where they happen to be located.

| Term | Plain meaning | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| Origin server | The original computer where content is permanently stored | Every new or uncached piece of content must eventually come from here |
| Edge location | A smaller computer placed near a group of people, holding copies of popular content | Shortens the physical distance data must travel, making loading faster |
| Cache hit | A moment when requested content is already available at a nearby edge location | Means faster delivery and less strain on the origin server |
| Cache miss | A moment when requested content is not yet stored at a nearby edge location | Triggers a fetch from the origin server, which takes longer |
